name: device_check
prose: Probes the eight SCSI IDs 0 to 7 in order for a PPA parallel-port device, using dev->base as the port base. Before each ID, if autodetect is true and the low three bits of dev->base are zero, dev->mode is set to PPA_EPP_8. For each ID it connects, tries ppa_select, and if that fails disconnects and moves on to the next ID. For the first ID that is selected it logs the ID and mode, writes a 6-byte all-zero test-unit-ready command with ppa_out one byte at a time (stopping at the first failing byte), then waits up to about 1 second for status bit 0x80 and checks that the top nibble of the status is 0xf0. Returns 0 when the command write and status check succeed (dev->mode is then whatever mode was in effect for that attempt, possibly the original mode after a retry). If the command write fails or the status top nibble is not 0xf0, it resets the bus (a reset pulse in the status case), and if dev->mode differs from the mode it had on entry it restores that mode and jumps back to re-select the same ID; the retry can then return -EIO, or can fail to select and continue with the next ID. If dev->mode already equals the entry mode when such a failure happens, it returns -EIO immediately with no retry; in the -EIO case dev->mode equals its entry value. Returns -ENODEV after all eight IDs when none produced a result; dev->mode at that point is the value set at the start of the last loop iteration (PPA_EPP_8 if autodetect and the low bits of dev->base are zero) unless the last iteration was a retry that failed to select, in which case it is the entry value. Performs port I/O, delays and printk; takes no locks and acquires or releases no memory.
note: Reviewer round 15 right (ENODEV after failed retry select at ppa.c:947-949 then 924-926 continue, mode restored at 948 and not re-set until next iteration 918-919); round 2 claim (no retry when mode==old_mode, ppa.c:947,951,970,974) was right and is covered.

name: qedf_send_rec
prose: Sends a REC (Read Exchange Concise) ELS for orig_io_req. Slice cut the head; this is the full function. Returns -EINVAL, taking no reference, if orig_io_req is NULL (checked first, before any dereference), if the QEDF_RPORT_SESSION_READY bit is clear in orig_io_req->fcport->flags, or if fcport->qedf is NULL. Otherwise it takes a kref on orig_io_req->refcount, reads the lport and sid, allocates a callback argument with kzalloc(GFP_NOIO), and if that fails returns -ENOMEM after dropping the reference with kref_put(qedf_release_cmd). With the argument allocated, it points cb_arg->aborted_io_req at orig_io_req, fills a fc_els_rec (source id, OX_ID from orig_io_req->xid, RX_ID from the task context) and calls qedf_initiate_els with qedf_rec_compl as the completion callback. If that call returns 0, the function returns 0 and keeps the reference and the cb_arg, which are intended for the completion path. If it returns nonzero, the function frees cb_arg, drops the reference with kref_put(qedf_release_cmd), and returns that value; qedf_initiate_els itself does not free cb_arg on its error paths (it can fail with -EINVAL, -EAGAIN, -ENOMEM and other codes). Logging is done on the error paths.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong on the NULL claim: qedf_els.c:1008-1011 does check orig_io_req == NULL and returns -EINVAL. Reviewer right-ish elsewhere only in that earlier prose assumed negative errno only; qedf_initiate_els error paths verified (no cb_arg free) in qedf_els.c:9-140. Slice cut the head.

name: qedi_show_boot_eth_info
prose:
Sysfs show callback for iSCSI boot ethernet attributes; data is the struct qedi_ctx. Slice cut the head. It calls qedi_get_nvram_block and returns 0 right away if that gives NULL. Otherwise it reads the IPv6-enabled and DHCP-enabled flags from the NVRAM block, selects the IP, subnet mask and gateway pointers and the format (static values from the initiator block, with ip_len = IPV6_LEN 41 or IPV4_LEN 17; when DHCP is enabled the strings "0::0" or "0.0.0.0" are used instead, with ip_len 5 or 8, and format "%s
"). Then by type: IP_ADDR, SUBNET_MASK and GATEWAY snprintf the chosen string into buf with limit ip_len; FLAGS and INDEX snprintf with limit 3; MAC calls sysfs_format_mac with qedi->mac; VLAN snprintfs the NVRAM VLAN field with limit 12; ORIGIN snprintfs "3
" with limit 3 only when DHCP is enabled; any other type sets rc to 0. The return value is rc: 0 if no NVRAM block or for an unhandled type, 1 (its initial value) for ORIGIN when DHCP is not enabled and nothing is written, and otherwise the return of snprintf (the length the untruncated output would have, which can exceed the limit) or of sysfs_format_mac. In DHCP mode the limits 5 and 8 are exactly the string length plus newline, so snprintf truncates and drops the trailing newline while still returning 5 or 8. No locks are taken and no memory or references are acquired or released in this function.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: static IP limit is IPV6_LEN/IPV4_LEN (qedi.h:362-363, qedi_main.c:2057), 5/8 only for DHCP (2068). Slice cut the head; real definition at qedi_main.c:2036.

name: __qedi_probe
prose: The slice is the body of __qedi_probe(pdev, mode), which qedi_probe calls as __qedi_probe(pdev, QEDI_MODE_NORMAL) (qedi_main.c:2851-2854); this entry describes __qedi_probe (slice cut the head). In non-recovery mode it allocates the host with qedi_host_alloc (NULL gives -ENOMEM); in recovery mode it reuses pci_get_drvdata(pdev) and sleeps 2 s before each probe attempt. It probes the qed device (qedi->cdev); if that returns NULL, in recovery mode it retries up to 10 times, otherwise or after that returns -ENODEV via free_host. It then fills dev info, sets iSCSI PF parameters (failure becomes -ENOMEM), prepares fastpath, starts the slowpath, sets up interrupts, programs BDQ doorbells, copies the MAC, starts LL2 (return value not checked) and, in non-recovery mode, starts the LL2 receive kthread (result not checked) and initialises locks, then starts the iSCSI function (failure gives -ENODEV). A set_link failure only logs a warning and marks the link down. When mode is QEDI_MODE_NORMAL it also adds the iSCSI host (failure -ENOMEM), allocates and initialises UIO rings, the cid queue, CM memory and the ITT table, creates the tmf and offload workqueues (failure -ENODEV), sets up boot info (failure only logged) and sends driver state to the MFW (failure only logged). Returns 0 at line 2798 when it gets there, else the error code of the first failing step, which is the callee's rc for fill_dev_info, qedi_prepare_fp, slowpath_start, qedi_setup_int, qedi_alloc_uio_rings, qedi_init_uio, qedi_setup_cid_que, qedi_cm_alloc_mem and qedi_alloc_itt. Error unwinding is a goto ladder (free_tmf_thread, free_cid_que, free_uio, remove_host, stop_iscsi_func, stop_slowpath, stop_hw, free_pf_params, free_host) that is not complete: the failures of qedi_alloc_itt, the tmf workqueue and the offload workqueue jump to free_cid_que or free_tmf_thread and do not free the CM memory from qedi_cm_alloc_mem (and, for the workqueue failures, not the ITT memory either); the failures at fill_dev_info and PF-param setup go straight to free_host without calling common->remove for the probed cdev; the unwind does not stop the LL2 receive thread or LL2; and in recovery mode the free_host label still calls iscsi_host_free on the reused host.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: qedi_alloc_itt failure (qedi_main.c:2752-2757) and tmf_thread failure (2762-2767) go to free_cid_que (2802) which skips any qedi_cm_alloc_mem release; earlier packet prose claimed wrapper qedi_probe releases everything. Slice is __qedi_probe, qedi_probe is the 4-line wrapper at 2851.

name: qla_zio_threshold_store
prose: Sysfs store handler for the ZIO threshold; vha comes from shost_priv(class_to_shost(dev)). Returns -EINVAL, changing nothing, if vha->hw->zio_mode is not QLA_ZIO_MODE_6, and -EINVAL if sscanf(buf, "%d", &val) does not convert exactly one integer (leading whitespace and a sign are accepted by sscanf). Returns -ERANGE, changing nothing, if val is below 0 or above 256. Otherwise it calls atomic_set(&vha->hw->zio_threshold, val) and returns strlen(buf) (not the count argument). It does not update last_zio_threshold and takes no lock; it acquires or releases no memory or references.
note: Name was wrong in the packet: the real function is qla_zio_threshold_store (qla_attr.c:1283-1297); no qla2x00_zio_threshold_store exists. Earlier prose matched the code (1289-1297); only the name failed the check.

name: qla25xx_fw_dump
prose: Captures an ISP25xx firmware dump into ha->fw_dump and returns void. Caller must hold ha->hardware_lock (lockdep_assert_held, qla_dbg.c:1338) and ha->fw_dump, when non-NULL, must be large enough for the isp25 dump and the chain data at ha->chain_offset, which the function does not bound-check. It first sets ha->fw_dump_cap_flags to 0. If ha->fw_dump is NULL it logs "No buffer available for dump" and returns; if ha->fw_dumped is already set it logs a warning and returns; both of these early returns skip the final qla2xxx_dump_post_process call. Otherwise it applies QLA_FW_STOPPED, prepares the header (qla2xxx_prep_dump, version set to 2), pauses the RISC and reads host status, host/RISC, PCIe, host-interface, shadow, RISC-I/O, mailbox, transfer/receive/auxiliary sequencer, command-DMA, request/response queue, transmit/receive DMA, RISC, local-memory-controller, FPM and frame-buffer registers into the isp25 section (also disabling interrupts via ictrl). It then copies the multi-queue chain entry with qla25xx_copy_mq into the chain area, and calls qla24xx_soft_reset; if that does not return QLA_SUCCESS it jumps to the end. It then dumps code RAM with qla24xx_dump_memory (a non-success result also jumps to the end), copies the queues and EFT, appends the FCE, multi-queue, ATIO-queue and extended-login chain entries, and if any chain entry was written sets DUMP_CHAIN_VARIANT in the version and DUMP_CHAIN_LAST on the last chain entry, and sets ha->fw_dump_len to the bytes used. On a soft-reset or dump-memory failure ha->fw_dump_len is not updated by this function. Every path that got past the two early returns calls qla2xxx_dump_post_process(base_vha, rval) with rval holding QLA_SUCCESS (the register reads and copies do not set rval) or the failing step's code.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong on both points: qla25xx_copy_mq is called at qla_dbg.c:1603 BEFORE qla24xx_soft_reset (1606), and FCE, mqueues, atioqueues and exlogin chain copies are at 1620-1623. Round 2 (size is only assumed, no bounds check, 1356-1358, 1603) right and kept in the precondition. Early-return paths 1345 and 1353 skip post_process, stated explicitly.

name: qla28xx_start_scsi_edif
prose: Builds and queues a Command Type 6 IOCB (with EDIF enabled) for the SCSI command in sp and returns QLA_SUCCESS or QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED. Slice cut the head. The caller does NOT hold the queue lock: the function itself takes sp->qpair->qp_lock_ptr with spin_lock_irqsave after an optional marker step. Steps: (1) if vha->marker_needed is set it calls qla2x00_marker; if that fails it logs and returns QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED with no lock taken and nothing to undo, otherwise it clears marker_needed. (2) It takes the lock, searches req->outstanding_cmds for a free handle starting after req->current_outstanding_cmd, and fails if none is found. (3) It maps the scatter/gather list with dma_map_sg (zero mapped entries is a failure; no sg list means zero segments), computes req_cnt, and gets firmware resources with qla_get_fw_resources, then makes sure the ring has req_cnt+2 free entries, rereading the out pointer once, else fails. (4) It gets an fcp_cmnd buffer with qla_get_buf (failure logged) and sets SRB_GOT_BUF in sp->flags; if cmd_len is above 16 and not a multiple of 4 it fails. (5) It fills the command packet, adds one DSD per segment with Continuation Type 1 packets as needed (none are added when there is no data transfer), updates the output or input byte and request counters and fcport->edif tx/rx bytes by direction, builds the FCP_CMND IU, then records sp in req->outstanding_cmds[handle], sets req->current_outstanding_cmd, sp->handle and cmd->host_scribble, subtracts req_cnt from req->cnt, advances the ring index and pointer (wrapping at req->length), increments sp->qpair->cmd_cnt, writes the new ring index to req->req_q_in, releases the lock with the saved flags and returns QLA_SUCCESS. Every failure after the lock is taken goes to one error label, which calls scsi_dma_unmap(cmd) if tot_dsds is nonzero, qla_put_buf on sp->u.scmd.buf_dsc, qla_put_fw_resources on sp->iores, releases the lock and returns QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED; that label runs qla_put_buf and qla_put_fw_resources even when the failure came before the buffer or resources were acquired, and it does not clear SRB_GOT_BUF.
note: Packet prose was wrong on a key point: it said the caller holds the lock, but the function takes it itself (qla_edif.c:3009-3010) and releases it at 3209 and 3220. Name qla28xx_start_scsi_edif at qla_edif.c:2969 (slice cut the head). Return paths: 3004, 3211, 3222.

name: qla24xx_async_gffid
prose: Sends a GFF_ID name-server query for fcport and waits for it. Returns QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED immediately, allocating nothing, when vha->flags.online is clear, when wait is false (no-wait is not handled), or when qla2x00_get_sp returns NULL. Otherwise it sets up the srb (SRB_CT_PTHRU_CMD, name "gffid", gen1/gen2 from fcport, completion callback qla24xx_async_gffid_sp_done, on-stack completion, SRB_WAKEUP_ON_COMP) and allocates a DMA-coherent CT request buffer and then a response buffer of sizeof(struct ct_sns_pkt) each. If either allocation fails it logs and jumps to the cleanup label with rval still QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED. After building the CT request it calls qla2x00_start_sp; a nonzero result sets rval to QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED and goes to cleanup. When start_sp succeeds it waits for the completion with wait_for_completion and returns sp->rc, which is whatever the done callback and the exchange left there (QLA_SUCCESS or another status). The cleanup label, reached on every path after the srb was obtained, frees the request and response buffers that were allocated, sets those pointers to NULL and drops the INIT reference with kref_put(&sp->cmd_kref, qla2x00_sp_release); the three early returns skip all of this.
note: All three reviewer claims right: early returns at qla_gs.c:2965-2966 and 2970-2971 happen before allocation/kref (round 2); DMA allocation failures (2990-2995, 2002-3007) and start_sp failure (3022-3024) occur with an srb already allocated and go through done_free_sp (round 15); sp->rc may be any status (3032, original).

name: qla_fab_async_scan
prose: Drives one stage of the fabric name-server scan (GPN_FT/GNN_FT for FCP, then NVMe). Slice cut the head. sp is either NULL (start a new scan) or the srb from the previous stage. Returns QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED without touching state if vha->flags.online is clear. Under vha->work_lock, if SF_SCANNING is already set it unlocks and goes to done_free_sp (which frees sp if non-NULL, then clears SF_SCANNING, sets SF_QUEUED and schedules scan.scan_work after 5 jiffies when scan_flags becomes 0, and returns the current rval, QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED here); otherwise it sets SF_SCANNING, and if sp is NULL forces scan.step to FAB_SCAN_START. A NULL sp therefore always takes the FAB_SCAN_START case. FAB_SCAN_START ignores any sp passed in, gets a new srb with qla2x00_get_sp, allocates a CT request buffer and a response buffer (sized from max_fibre_devices), zeroes the scan list and sets step to FAB_SCAN_GPNFT_FCP; if get_sp or either DMA allocation fails it clears SF_SCANNING, frees what it obtained (the request buffer and srb on a response failure, the srb on a request failure) and returns QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED. A non-NULL sp passed in at the START step is not released by this function. The FAB_SCAN_GPNFT_FCP, GNNFT_FCP and GPNFT_NVME cases only advance step to the next stage. FAB_SCAN_GNNFT_NVME and unknown steps do WARN_ON(1) and go to done_free_sp. If the srb's request or response buffer is missing, it clears SF_SCANNING, WARN_ONs, sets LOCAL_LOOP_UPDATE and LOOP_RESYNC_NEEDED in dpc_flags and goes to done_free_sp. Otherwise it zeroes both buffers, initialises the srb (SRB_CT_PTHRU_CMD, callback qla_async_scan_sp_done), prepares the CT preamble for the current step (GPN_FT or GNN_FT with FC4_TYPE_FCP_SCSI for the FCP steps or FC4_TYPE_NVME for the NVMe steps), sets nport_handle to NPH_SNS and calls qla2x00_start_sp. If start_sp returns QLA_SUCCESS the function returns it and leaves the srb to the completion callback with SF_SCANNING still set; otherwise it goes to done_free_sp and returns start_sp's nonzero value. The final step of done_free_sp clears SF_SCANNING even when the flag was set by another scan.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: sp==NULL forces step=START at qla_gs.c:3539-3540, so the NULL-sp-at-later-step behavior in the old prose is unreachable (the !sp check at 3622 cannot trigger). Original reviewer right: default case (3615-3619) goes to done_free_sp which clears SF_SCANNING (3722), but old prose was inconsistent. Also found: caller sp is overwritten at 3550 for START.

name: qla24xx_handle_prli_done_event
prose: Handles the completion of an async PRLI for ea->fcport; returns void. Slice cut the head. It first does WARN_ONCE if ea->data[0] is not a valid mailbox status, then switches on ea->data[0]. For MBS_COMMAND_COMPLETE it sets fcport->chip_reset from vha->hw->base_qpair->chip_reset, sets logout_on_delete to 1, stores ea->iop[0] in nvme_prli_service_param, sets nvme_first_burst_size to (ea->iop[1] & 0xffff) * 512 when ea->iop[0] has NVME_PRLI_SP_FIRST_BURST and to 0 otherwise, and calls qla24xx_post_gpdb_work. For any other status it reads ea->sp and updates fcport->do_prli_nvme: if NVME_FCP_TARGET(fcport) it is set to 0 when the logio flags of ea->sp contain SRB_LOGIN_NVME_PRLI and to 1 when they do not, and if the port is not an NVME_FCP_TARGET it is set to 0. Then, in N2N topology: if n2n_link_reset_cnt equals vha->hw->login_retry_count and FCF_FCSP_DEVICE is set it is reset to 0; then if n2n_link_reset_cnt is below login_retry_count it is incremented, vha->relogin_jif is set to jiffies + 2*HZ, N2N_LINK_RESET is set in dpc_flags and the DPC is woken; otherwise only a warning "Unable to reconnect" is logged. In non-N2N topology it clears FCF_ASYNC_SENT, sets keep_nport_handle to 0 and logout_on_delete to 1, and calls qlt_schedule_sess_for_deletion. No locks are taken here and nothing is allocated.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: do_prli_nvme = 1 when SRB_LOGIN_NVME_PRLI is absent (qla_init.c:2420-2424); old prose said the reverse. Original and round-2 claims were about the N2N paths, now enumerated (2429-2452).

name: qla2x00_configure_local_loop
prose: Refreshes vha->vp_fcports from the adapter's local-loop ID list. Slice cut the head; real definition at qla_init.c:5900. Return paths: (1) if N2N_TOPO(ha) it returns the result of qla2x00_configure_n2n_loop(vha) at once. (2) It clears ha->gid_list and calls qla2x00_get_id_list; a failure returns that error code (goto err, no temporary fcport exists yet). (3) If the returned entry count is 0 it increments vha->scan.scan_retry under vha->work_lock; if scan_retry is still below MAX_SCAN_RETRIES it asks qla2x00_get_fcal_position_map, and if that succeeds with more than 1 map entry it calls qla_reinitialize_link and returns QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED; otherwise it sets LOCAL_LOOP_UPDATE and LOOP_RESYNC_NEEDED in dpc_flags and carries on with the scan; at or above MAX_SCAN_RETRIES it carries on without setting flags. A non-zero entry count resets scan_retry to 0. (4) It marks every fcport on vp_fcports as QLA_FCPORT_SCAN and allocates a temporary fcport; allocation failure returns QLA_MEMORY_ALLOC_FAILED. (5) For each ID-list entry it skips reserved domains (top nibble 0xf), entries on another domain/area when topology is ISP_CFG_NL, and loop IDs above LAST_LOCAL_LOOP_ID; for others it fills the temporary fcport (marked QLA_FCPORT_FOUND) and calls qla2x00_get_port_database. If that fails, it sets LOOP_RESYNC_NEEDED and skips the entry unless ha->current_topology is ISP_CFG_N, where it continues with the match step anyway. Under tgt.sess_lock it looks for an existing fcport with the same port_name: a match is updated (loop_id, port_type, d_id, node_name, FOUND, login_retry reloaded when 0); no match adds the temporary fcport to vp_fcports and allocates a replacement, and if that allocation fails it returns QLA_MEMORY_ALLOC_FAILED at once (no temporary fcport is held then, and fcports already added stay on the list). fp_speed is set from ha->link_data_rate. (6) After the loop it walks vp_fcports (stopping if LOOP_RESYNC_NEEDED is set): ports still in SCAN state that are online in initiator/dual mode are marked lost and some are scheduled for deletion via qlt_schedule_sess_for_deletion; ports in FOUND state get qla24xx_fcport_handle_login. Then it frees the last temporary fcport with qla2x00_free_fcport and returns rval, which is the QLA_SUCCESS from get_id_list at that point. Entries whose port database read failed are therefore not marked FOUND, and the function can still return QLA_SUCCESS.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: get_port_database failure sets LOOP_RESYNC_NEEDED and continues (qla_init.c:6008-6019), the function still returns rval == QLA_SUCCESS (6108); old prose said every discovered port ends FOUND. Slice cut the head. Also corrected: err returns never hold an unfreed temporary fcport (NULL at 5968 and 6065).

name: qla_start_scsi_type6
prose: Queues a Command Type 6 IOCB for the SCSI command in sp (qla_iocb.c:4247); the packet name qla24xx_build_scsi_iocbs_ring_entry does not exist, and the slice is only the later part of this function. The function takes qpair->qp_lock itself with spin_lock_irqsave and every return releases it. If vha->marker_needed is set it calls __qla2x00_marker; a failure unlocks and returns QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED with nothing to undo, otherwise marker_needed is cleared. It gets a handle from qla2xxx_get_next_handle (0 means none and fails), maps the sg list with dma_map_sg (zero entries fails), computes req_cnt, acquires firmware resources with qla_get_fw_resources, checks the DSD chain budget (more_dsd_lists plus qpair->dsd_inuse must stay below NUM_DSD_CHAIN), allocates extra DSD list entries with kzalloc(GFP_ATOMIC) and dma_pool_alloc as needed (added to qpair->dsd_list and counted in dsd_avail), then checks ring space (re-reading the out pointer; a register disconnect or still-too-small ring fails) and allocates the FCP_CMND buffer from ha->fcp_cmnd_dma_pool. If cmd_len is above 16 and is not a multiple of 4 or exceeds QLA_CDB_BUF_SIZE it fails via the label that also frees the FCP_CMND buffer. On success path it records sp in req->outstanding_cmds[handle], sets req->current_outstanding_cmd, sp->handle and cmd->host_scribble, decrements req->cnt, builds the type 6 packet through qla24xx_build_scsi_type_6_iocbs, fills the FCP_CMND IU (LUN, direction bits, priority, CDB, FCP_DL), sets SRB_FCP_CMND_DMA_VALID, advances the ring index (wrapping at req->length), increments qpair->cmd_cnt, sets SRB_DMA_VALID, writes the ring index to req->req_q_in, processes the response queue if vha->flags.process_response_queue is set and the next response entry is not yet marked processed, unlocks and returns QLA_SUCCESS. Failure labels unwind in order: the FCP_CMND buffer is returned to the pool (only on the cmd_len failure path, since the later label alone does not free it); then scsi_dma_unmap if tot_dsds is nonzero; qla_put_fw_resources on sp->iores (also on failures before qla_get_fw_resources ran); freeing sp->u.scmd.crc_ctx to ha->ctx_mempool if set; unlock; return QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED. The failure at the FCP_CMND allocation and ring-space checks goes to the plain error label and DSD list entries already added to qpair->dsd_list are not freed there.
note: Name wrong in packet: real function is qla_start_scsi_type6 (qla_iocb.c:4247-4502); the slice 4384-4502 starts mid-function. Old prose wrong on: failure label does not free the FCP CMND buffer except on the cmd_len path (4485-4486 vs 4488); SRB_FCP_CMND_DMA_VALID set only at 4455.

name: qla2x00_async_event
prose: Processes one firmware asynchronous event; mb holds the event code in mb[0] and its parameters, and the caller must pass a writable array of at least 8 uint16_t because some cases store mb[4] to mb[7] (and mb[0] is rewritten). Slice cut the head; real definition at qla_isr.c:1258. If ha->flags.fw_started is clear it logs and returns immediately without calling the later steps. Otherwise, unless IS_CNA_CAPABLE(ha), a first switch decodes the fast-post completion codes (MBA_SCSI_COMPLETION, MBA_CMPLT_1_16BIT to _5_16BIT, MBA_CMPLT_2_32BIT) into up to five handles and rewrites mb[0] to MBA_SCSI_COMPLETION for all but MBA_SCSI_COMPLETION itself. A second switch on mb[0] then handles the event: for fast-post completions, if vha->flags.online it calls qla2x00_process_completed_request for each handle; for reset, system error (increments hw_err_cnt, dumps firmware, marks it stopped, then either takes the adapter offline with DFLG_DEV_FAILED or sets ISP_ABORT_NEEDED and possibly MPI_RESET_NEEDED), transfer errors, loop init error, LIP, loop up, loop down, LIP reset, point-to-point, change in connection, port update and RSCN it adjusts loop_state, loop_down_timer, vp_state, dpc_flags, link data rate and devices-lost state and posts AEN work as the event requires; further cases handle congestion notification, ZIO response, ISP84xx alerts, DCBX, IDC (IDC_NOTIFY falls through to IDC_COMPLETE and IDC_TIME_EXT), IDC AEN (stores mb[4..7] on QLA83xx), D-Port diagnostics, temperature alert, and SFP insert/remove. Several cases leave the switch early with break (for example online check, ISP2100, RSCN for another vport); no case returns from the function, whose only return is the fw_started check. name: qla2x00_mailbox_command
prose: Issues one mailbox command described by mcp (mcp->mb[0] command, out_mb/in_mb register masks, tov timeout in seconds, flags) and waits for the firmware. Slice cut the head; real definition at qla_mbx.c:106. The caller must not hold ha->hardware_lock; the function takes and releases it in short sections. Early returns before the command slot is taken, each returning QLA_FUNCTION_TIMEOUT without clearing any flag: the PCI channel is in the permanent-failure state or ha->flags.pci_channel_io_perm_failure is set, vha->device_flags has DFLG_DEV_FAILED, the base vha has both PFLG_DISCONNECTED and UNLOADING set, the 82xx firmware is already hung (this also sets mcp->mb[0] to MBS_LINK_DOWN_ERROR), an ISP abort is active, retrying or needed and the command is not a ROM command, or ha->flags.eeh_busy is set. Then it increments num_pend_mbx_stage1 and waits up to tov seconds for ha->mbx_cmd_comp; on timeout it increments hw_err_cnt, decrements the counter and returns QLA_FUNCTION_TIMEOUT. After getting the slot, if purge_mbox is set, the chip_reset count has changed or eeh_busy is set it sets rval to QLA_ABORTED and goes to premature_exit. Otherwise it sets ha->mcp, takes the hardware lock, re-checks purge_mbox, chip_reset and mbox_busy (QLA_ABORTED and premature_exit if any), sets mbox_busy, writes the out_mb registers, raises the host interrupt and waits either on mbx_intr_comp (interrupt mode) or by polling qla2x00_poll up to tov seconds. A purge or chip reset seen while waiting clears mbox_busy, adjusts the stage2 counter and gives QLA_ABORTED via premature_exit; on 82xx in polling mode a hint bit that is still pending clears mbox_busy and gives QLA_FUNCTION_TIMEOUT via premature_exit. If the firmware signalled completion: when the 82xx firmware is hung it clears mbox_busy, sets mcp->mb[0] to MBS_LINK_DOWN_ERROR, sets ha->mcp to NULL, and returns QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED via premature_exit with the in_mb registers not copied; if mailbox_out[0] is not MBS_COMMAND_COMPLETE rval becomes QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED; in both the success and this failed-status case the in_mb registers are copied from ha->mailbox_out into mcp->mb. If no completion came, it logs registers; if the PCI channel is not offline it checks the device, and if the vendor ID reads 0xffff, ictrl reads all ones or chip_reset changed it clears mbox_busy and returns QLA_FUNCTION_TIMEOUT via premature_exit, otherwise it dumps the firmware (unless the command is MBC_GEN_SYSTEM_ERROR) and sets QLA_FUNCTION_TIMEOUT; if the PCI channel is offline, rval is left at QLA_SUCCESS. After the wait (reached unless premature_exit was taken) it clears mbox_busy, sets ha->mcp to NULL, optionally polls the response queue, and for QLA_FUNCTION_TIMEOUT with a command other than MBC_GEN_SYSTEM_ERROR it either sets ISP_ABORT_NEEDED and wakes the DPC (when io lock is off, an IOCTL command or eeh_busy, unless an abort is already pending) or, if running in the DPC thread, runs abort_isp inline (completing mbx_cmd_comp first and skipping the later complete); other callers get no abort. premature_exit completes ha->mbx_cmd_comp, and every path then logs a failure for nonzero rval and returns rval after an optional bounded EEH delay. The QLA_ABORTED path from the second re-check (after the lock is taken) leaves ha->mcp set to mcp and does not reset it here; the first re-check path returns before ha->mcp is set. Possible return values are QLA_SUCCESS, QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED, QLA_FUNCTION_TIMEOUT and QLA_ABORTED.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: the prose already separated the two 82xx cases and the code agrees: hung before the command returns TIMEOUT (qla_mbx.c:159-164), hung after completion returns FAILED with mb[0] set (379-390). The old prose was wrong elsewhere: it said mbox_busy/ha->mcp are reset on every path that took the lock, but the ABORTED path at 212-217 leaves ha->mcp set (205) and does not touch mbox_busy, while the earlier ABORTED path at 194-201 returns before ha->mcp is set. name: qla_adjust_buf
prose: Periodic buffer-pool adjustment for the base host; the slice cut the head, the function is qla_adjust_buf (qla_mid.c:1278). It returns immediately if vha->vp_idx is nonzero. If vha->buf_expired is 0 it sets it to jiffies + EXPIRE (60 * HZ) and returns. If jiffies is still before buf_expired (time_before) it returns. Otherwise it sets buf_expired to jiffies + EXPIRE and loops over qpair indexes 0 to vha->hw->num_qpairs - 1: for each non-NULL qpair in vha->hw->queue_pair_map whose buf_pool.num_alloc is nonzero, if buf_pool.take_snapshot is already set it takes the qpair lock (spin_lock_irqsave on qp->qp_lock_ptr), calls __qla_adjust_buf(qp) and releases the lock; if it is not set it sets take_snapshot to 1 without taking the lock. Qpairs that are NULL or have num_alloc equal to 0 are skipped. The function returns void; no locks are held when it returns, and it allocates nothing and takes no references.

name: qlafx00_iospace_config
prose: Reserves and maps the PCI regions of a FX00 adapter. Slice cut the head. It calls pci_request_selected_regions(ha->pdev, ha->bars, QLA2XXX_DRIVER_NAME). It then requires BAR 0 to have IORESOURCE_MEM set and pci_resource_len of at least BAR0_LEN_FX00, and maps BAR 0 with ioremap into ha->cregbase; then requires BAR 2 to be IORESOURCE_MEM and at least BAR2_LEN_FX00 long, and maps it into ha->iobase. Finally it sets ha->max_req_queues and ha->max_rsp_queues to 1, logs the BAR values and returns 0. Every failure (region reservation fails, BAR 0 not MMIO, BAR 0 too short, ioremap of BAR 0 fails, BAR 2 not MMIO, BAR 2 too short, ioremap of BAR 2 fails) goes to one label that returns -ENOMEM. On failure it does not release the regions or iounmap anything already mapped (for example cregbase stays mapped if the BAR 2 checks fail), and max_req_queues and max_rsp_queues are left unchanged.

name: qla2xxx_process_purls_iocb
prose: Handles an unsolicited received FC-NVMe LS (PURLS) IOCB; the packet name was a placeholder, the function is qla2xxx_process_purls_iocb(void **pkt, struct rsp_que **rsp) (qla_nvme.c:1253, slice cut the head). It finds the vha with qla2xxx_get_vha_from_vp_idx(ha, p->vp_index); if none, it logs a warning, does WARN_ON_ONCE(1) and returns without sending a reject and without consuming the IOCB. Otherwise it builds a reject argument (opcode byte, vp index, nport handle, ox_id, exchange address) and looks up the fcport by source port id with qla2x00_find_fcport_by_nportid. If no fcport is found it sets reason FCNVME_RJT_RC_INV_ASSOC and marks a reject to be sent. If found, it reads fcport->nvme_remote_port and its private data without a NULL check, then calls qla27xx_copy_multiple_pkt(vha, pkt, rsp, true, false) to copy the IOCB (that function marks the head IOCB processed and consumes continuation IOCBs itself when it gets as far as copying); if it returns NULL it sets reason FCNVME_RJT_RC_LOGIC and marks a reject. It then allocates a qla_nvme_unsol_ctx with kzalloc(GFP_ATOMIC); if that fails it frees the copied item with qla24xx_free_purex_item, sets reason FCNVME_RJT_RC_LOGIC and marks a reject. On success it fills the uctx, stores it in qla_rport->uctx, adds it to fcport->unsol_ctx_head under fcport->unsol_ctx_lock, sets item->purls_context to it and queues the item with qla24xx_queue_purex_item to run qla2xxx_process_purls_pkt. At the common exit, if a reject was marked it calls qla_nvme_ls_reject_iocb on (*rsp)->qpair and then __qla_consume_iocb, which in the uctx-failure case runs after the copy step has already marked the head processed. The function returns void.

name: qla8044_poll_wait_for_ready
prose: Polls an indirect CRB register until a mask is set. It computes a deadline of jiffies + msecs_to_jiffies(TIMEOUT_100_MS), then loops: each pass calls qla8044_rd_reg_indirect(vha, addr1, &temp) (its return value is ignored, and temp starts at 0, so a failed read leaves the previous value in temp), and if (temp & mask) is nonzero it leaves the loop and the function returns 0. Otherwise, if time_after_eq(jiffies, timeout), it logs a warning ("Error in processing rdmdio entry") and returns -1. There are no other return values. The success test runs before the timeout test in every pass, so a read taken after the deadline has passed still counts as success if its masked bits are nonzero; there is no delay between reads. Takes no locks and allocates nothing.

name: qla2x00_probe_one
prose: PCI probe for a QLogic ISP adapter; slice cut the head, real definition at qla_os.c:2904 with ret initialised to -ENODEV. Early failures return ret (-ENODEV) without unwinding: pci_enable_device_mem or pci_enable_device failing returns at once; kzalloc of the qla_hw_data failing, or qla_edif_sadb_build_free_pool failing (which first kfrees ha), goes to disable_device, which calls pci_disable_device and returns -ENODEV. It then selects ISP-specific parameters, calls isp_ops->iospace_config (a nonzero result goes to iospace_config_failed with that errno), qla2x00_mem_alloc (failure goes to probe_hw_failed with its errno), qla2x00_create_host (NULL gives -ENOMEM via probe_hw_failed), sets drvdata and PFLG_DRIVER_PROBING, then requests IRQs (error to probe_failed with its errno), allocates queues (-ENODEV to probe_failed), allocates the ha->wq workqueue (-ENOMEM to probe_failed), calls isp_ops->initialize_adapter (nonzero marks 82xx/8044 device state failed under the IDC lock and returns -ENODEV via probe_failed), creates qpairs when mqenable, and, unless ha->flags.running_gold_fw is set (which jumps to skip_dpc), creates the DPC kthread with kthread_create (failure gives PTR_ERR via probe_failed). Later it calls scsi_add_host; a nonzero result goes to probe_failed with that errno. After scsi_add_host it sets init_done and online, scans or enumerates, allocates sysfs attrs, initialises host attributes, sets up debugfs and the target, and clears PFLG_DRIVER_PROBING. It then returns -ENODEV if UNLOADING is set in the base vha's dpc_flags at that point (the adapter is not unwound in that case), else 0. UNLOADING is checked only once, after registration. On success the DPC thread exists unless running_gold_fw skipped its creation. The unwind labels run in order: probe_failed stops edif and edb work, frees scan and gnl buffers, stops the timer if active, sets online to 0, stops the DPC thread if present, calls qla2x00_free_device and scsi_host_put, and clears the local req/rsp pointers; probe_hw_failed then frees memory and the request/response queues and clears driver-active; iospace_config_failed unmaps the register mappings (the P3P branch tests !ha->nx_pcibase and !ql2xdbwr before iounmap), releases the PCI regions and kfrees ha; disable_device disables the PCI device and returns ret. The ha->wq workqueue is not destroyed explicitly in the labels shown here.

Old prose also wrong in claiming UNLOADING is checked before registration: only one check, at 3614. name: qla2x00_mem_alloc
prose: Allocates the adapter's memory resources (qla2x00_mem_alloc, defined at qla_os.c:4145; the slice cut the head). In order it allocates, as applicable: ha->vp_map (only when target mode or EDIF is enabled), the init control block (DMA coherent), the host_map btree, target memory via qlt_mem_alloc, the gid_list, the SRB mempool, a ct6_dsd cache and ctx mempool (for P3P, QLA27xx, or QLA28xx with ql2xsecenable), the NVRAM buffer, the s_dma_pool, and, for P3P, ql2xenabledif or QLA28xx with ql2xsecenable, the dl_dma_pool, fcp_cmnd_dma_pool and, when ql2xenabledif is set, the dif_bundl_pool with up to 128 pre-allocated dsd entries, then either the SNS command buffer (QLA2100/2200) or the MS IOCB and CT SNS buffer, the request queue and its ring, the response queue and its ring (cross-linked through (*req)->rsp and (*rsp)->req), npiv_info when nvram_npiv_size is nonzero, the extended and secure-fabric init control blocks, async_pd (non-FWI2), the loop-ID bitmap, SFP data, the flash layout table, the purex DMA pool, and the ELS reject and FC-NVMe LS reject DMA buffers. It returns 0 at line 4484 once all of these succeed. Every failure jumps to a fail_* label that releases, in reverse order, what was acquired earlier (including the queues and rings through kfree of *req and *rsp), and the final label returns -ENOMEM. Two paths differ from that pattern: if kzalloc of one DIF-bundling dsd fails the function returns -ENOMEM directly without unwinding (qla_os.c:4253), and if dma_pool_alloc for a dsd's DMA address fails that dsd is freed and the loop continues, so the allocation as a whole is not failed (4260-4267). Dsd entries on the good list are freed again after the loop (4288-4296); entries on the unusable list are kept until the failure unwind or later teardown. Takes no locks.

name: qla24xx_create_new_sess
prose: Work handler for a QLA_EVT_NEW_SESS event; returns void. Slice cut the head; real definition at qla_os.c:5307. e->u.new_sess carries port_name, id, node_name, fc4_type and an optional pla (PLOGI ack). Under tgt.sess_lock it looks up an fcport by WWPN. If one exists it sets its d_id from the event and, when pla is non-NULL, sets fw_login_state to DSC_LS_PLOGI_PEND, copies the pla's node name, links pla to the fcport (qlt_plogi_ack_link) and decrements pla->ref_count. If none exists it drops the lock and allocates one with qla2x00_alloc_fcport; if that fails it frees pla (list_del and kmem_cache_free to qla_tgt_plogi_cachep) when pla is non-NULL and returns, creating nothing. A new fcport gets d_id, FCF_FABRIC_DEVICE, port_name, fc4_type, do_prli_nvme and, for FS_FCP_IS_N2N event types, N2N timing/flags; then under the lock the WWPN is looked up again. If another fcport now exists (a duplicate), the new one is marked to be freed and not added; otherwise it is added to vha->vp_fcports. With pla non-NULL it is linked and ref_count decremented as above. After unlocking, if there is an fcport it sets id_changed, scan_state QLA_FCPORT_FOUND, chip_reset from the base qpair and node_name from the event. If pla is non-NULL and its status_subcode is ELS_PRLI it applies the PRLI-derived fields (login state, loop_id from the nport handle, conf_compl_supported from wd3_lo BIT_7, port_type FCT_TARGET if BIT_4 set else FCT_INITIATOR); in either pla case it then calls qlt_plogi_ack_unref. If pla is NULL it looks up an fcport by NportID under the lock; if one exists other than this fcport: state DSC_DELETED changes nothing, DSC_DELETE_PEND sets fcport->login_pause and tfcp->conflict = fcport, and any other state does the same and additionally calls qlt_schedule_sess_for_deletion on that fcport after the lock is released. Then, still only for pla NULL, in N2N topology it clears FCF_FABRIC_DEVICE, sets keep_nport_handle and possibly NVMe fc4_type and n2n_flag, resets fw_login_state to 0 and schedules scan_work after 5 jiffies, and otherwise calls qla24xx_fcport_handle_login. Finally, if the new fcport was a duplicate it is freed with qla2x00_free_fcport and pla, when non-NULL, is removed from its list and freed.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: DSC_DELETED case sets neither conflict nor login_pause (qla_os.c:5442-5443); old prose lumped DELETE_PEND with DELETED. Also corrected: N2N handling / qla24xx_fcport_handle_login only runs when pla is NULL (5426-5472), and DELETE_PEND sets both fields without scheduling deletion (5444-5447). Original reviewer (alloc-failure path) right and covered (5361-5370). Slice cut the head.

name: qla24xx_read_fcp_prio_cfg
prose: Reads the FCP priority configuration from flash into ha->fcp_prio_cfg. If ha->fcp_prio_cfg is NULL it vmallocs FCP_PRIO_CFG_SIZE bytes; if that fails it logs and returns QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED with nothing else changed. It zeroes the whole buffer, then reads the header (FCP_PRIO_CFG_HDR_SIZE bytes) from flash word address ha->flt_region_fcp_prio (shifted left by 2) with ha->isp_ops->read_optrom (whose return value is not checked) and validates it with qla24xx_fcp_prio_cfg_valid(..., 0). If the header is invalid it goes to the failure label. Otherwise it reads the entries, min(num_entries * sizeof(struct qla_fcp_prio_entry), FCP_PRIO_CFG_SIZE - FCP_PRIO_CFG_HDR_SIZE) bytes starting at the entry array, and revalidates the whole configuration with qla24xx_fcp_prio_cfg_valid(..., 1). If that passes, it sets ha->flags.fcp_prio_enabled to 1 and returns QLA_SUCCESS, leaving the buffer allocated. At the failure label it vfrees ha->fcp_prio_cfg, sets it to NULL, leaves fcp_prio_enabled unchanged and returns QLA_FUNCTION_FAILED. Whether the buffer exists on entry does not matter: it is allocated here when NULL (and reused, after zeroing, when already allocated).
note: Name was wrong: real function is qla24xx_read_fcp_prio_cfg (qla_sup.c:3638-3682); old prose wrongly required the buffer to be pre-allocated, but lines 3644-3652 allocate it and return FAILED if vmalloc fails. Returns at 3650, 3677, 3681.

name: qla2xxx_get_flt_info
prose: Fills the ha->flt_region_* flash address fields from the flash layout table (FLT) at flt_addr; returns void (qla_sup.c:653, slice cut the head). ha->flt must point to a buffer of at least sizeof(struct qla_flt_header) + FLT_REGIONS_SIZE bytes. It selects def = 2 for QLA81XX, 1 for QLA25XX, else 0; sets ha->flt_region_fcp_prio from the port-0 or port-1 default table (fcp_prio_cfg0 or fcp_prio_cfg1 [def], chosen by ha->port_no == 0) and ha->flt_region_flt = flt_addr, then reads the header and region area into ha->flt with isp_ops->read_optrom (result not checked). If the first 16-bit word is 0xffff, or flt->version is not 1, or the 16-bit word sum over sizeof(*flt) + flt->length bytes is nonzero, it goes to no_flash_data, where it sets flt_region_fw, flt_region_boot, flt_region_vpd_nvram and flt_region_fdt from def_fw, def_boot, def_vpd_nvram and def_fdt [def], and flt_region_vpd, flt_region_nvram and flt_region_npiv_conf from the port-0 or port-1 default tables chosen by port_no == 0, leaving all other flt_region_* fields unchanged. Otherwise it walks flt->length / sizeof(region) entries (the count comes from the flash data and is not compared against FLT_REGIONS_SIZE) and, for each entry, a switch on the region code stores start = region->start >> 2 in the matching field (fw, boot, vpd_nvram, vpd, nvram, fdt, npiv_conf, gold_fw, fcp_prio, bootload, img_status_pri/sec, fw_sec, boot_sec, aux_img_status_pri/sec, nvram_sec, vpd_nvram_sec, vpd_sec), only when that code's adapter-type and port_no conditions hold; entries with unknown codes or failed conditions change nothing, and fields with no applicable entry keep their previous value. In both paths it finishes by logging the resulting values. It takes no lock and allocates nothing.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong for this tree: the FLT buffer is ha->flt (qla_sup.c:688 flt = ha->flt; 701-703 read_optrom into flt), not req->ring. Prose precondition about ha->flt kept; added the unchecked count from flt->length (726) and the unchecked read_optrom result.

name: qlt_do_ctio_completion
prose: Completes a target-mode CTIO for a command; returns void (qla_target.c:3912, slice cut the head). If handle has CTIO_INTERMEDIATE_HANDLE_MARK it only logs when status is not CTIO_SUCCESS and returns. Otherwise it calls qlt_ctio_to_cmd(vha, rsp, handle, ctio), which returns NULL for the skip handle, an unknown queue id, an out-of-range handle, an empty outstanding_cmds slot, or the null handle, and otherwise returns the command and clears its slot in req->outstanding_cmds; a NULL result makes this function return. For a resolved command, ctio is dereferenced unconditionally (to read the CTIO7 flags at line 3934), so ctio must be non-NULL whenever the handle resolves to a command. If those flags contain CTIO7_FLAGS_DATA_OUT and cmd->sess is set it calls qlt_chk_edif_rx_sa_delete_pending. It sets cmd->cmd_sent_to_fw to 0 and unmaps the SG list (qlt_unmap_sg). If status is not CTIO_SUCCESS a switch on the low 16 bits of the status logs the cause; for CTIO_PORT_LOGGED_OUT with cmd->sess set it also sets send_els_logo and schedules the session for deletion, and CTIO_PORT_UNAVAILABLE logs only; CTIO_DIF_ERROR calls qlt_handle_dif_error and returns without freeing the command in this function. For other error statuses, if the command is neither in QLA_TGT_STATE_NEED_DATA nor aborted it sets TRC_CTIO_ERR and returns if qlt_term_ctio_exchange returns nonzero. Next: state QLA_TGT_STATE_PROCESSED sets TRC_CTIO_DONE; QLA_TGT_STATE_NEED_DATA moves the command to QLA_TGT_STATE_DATA_IN, sets write_data_transferred when status is CTIO_SUCCESS, calls tgt_ops->handle_data(cmd) and returns; an aborted command sets TRC_CTIO_ABORTED; anything else sets TRC_CTIO_STRANGE. For the paths that continue, a non-success status on a non-aborted command emits dump_stack(), and finally tgt_ops->free_cmd(cmd) is called. The function itself takes no locks; whether callees (handle_data, free_cmd, qlt_term_ctio_exchange) drop or retake ha->hardware_lock was not verified.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: ctio is dereferenced at qla_target.c:3934 for every resolved command, so it cannot be NULL then; qlt_ctio_to_cmd returns NULL for the null handle either way (3882-3904), so a NULL ctio never gets past 3931 only when the handle is the null handle. Original claim (invalid handles handled) was also right and is in the prose; the claim 'may drop and reacquire the lock' in the old prose is unverified and removed.

name: qlt_handle_login
prose: Handles an incoming PLOGI/PRLI immediate-notify iocb in target mode; returns int (qla_target.c:4684, slice cut the head). The caller must hold vha->hw->hardware_lock (lockdep_assert_held). It reads the WWN, port_id and loop_id from the iocb and first calls abort_cmds_for_s_id, which takes vha->cmd_list_lock internally. If the WWN is nonzero it takes tgt.sess_lock and calls qlt_find_sess_invalidate_other(vha, wwn, port_id, loop_id, &conflict_sess), which can already modify other sessions (for example it may set keep_nport_handle on or schedule deletion of an other session) and sets sess and conflict_sess; if the WWN is zero it sends a terminating immediate notify (qlt_send_term_imm_notif) and returns 0. Then, if IS_SW_RESV_ADDR(port_id) it sets res = 1 and returns 1 without sending a terminate, posting work or touching sess in this function (the earlier invalidate step may have changed other sessions). Every other exit returns res = 0. With edif enabled, it sends a terminating notify and returns 0 when the doorbell is not active and the PLOGI lacks the FCSP flag, or when DBELL_INACTIVE, or for a PLOGI without FCSP. It then calls qlt_plogi_ack_find_add; NULL gives a terminating notify and return 0. If conflict_sess exists it increments its login_gen and links the plogi ack to it as a conflict. If no session was found it increments pla->ref_count and posts new-session work with qla24xx_post_newsess_work (with the node name for PLOGI, NULL otherwise), then returns 0. If the found session is in DSC_UPD_FCPORT it sets next_disc_state to DSC_DELETE_PEND, frees the plogi ack (list_del and kmem_cache_free) only when there is no conflict_sess, sends a terminating notify and returns 0. Otherwise it links the plogi ack to the session, sets d_id, login_gen++ and loop_id from the iocb, does N2N d_id and AEN handling for PLOGI, sets fw_login_state to PRLI pending (also setting local, conf_compl_supported from wd3_lo BIT_7 and port_type from BIT_4) for PRLI or PLOGI pending otherwise, and switches on sess->disc_state: DSC_DELETED and DSC_LOGIN_PEND call qlt_plogi_ack_unref; any other state sets keep_nport_handle from comparing the session loop_id and d_id with the iocb values (equal at that point, because they were assigned from the iocb above) and calls qlt_schedule_sess_for_deletion. Then it returns 0.
note: Reviewer rounds original/2/15 all right: the return-1 path (qla_target.c:4722-4724) is reached only after qlt_find_sess_invalidate_other at 4711, which can change other sessions, so 'no session updated' was too strong. Slice cut the head. Also verified abort_cmds_for_s_id takes cmd_list_lock (4661-4679).

name: qla4xxx_set_ipv6
prose: Applies one iSCSI network parameter (iface_param->param, value, len, iface_num) to the IPv6 part of the address control block init_fw_cb; returns void (ql4_os.c:2035, slice cut the head). It is a switch with exactly one case taken. The cases IPV6_ADDR, IFACE_ENABLE, VLAN_TAG, VLAN_ENABLED and MTU have no iface_num guard; every other recognised case does nothing when iface_param->iface_num is odd (IPV6_ADDR instead picks ipv6_addr1 for odd iface_num and ipv6_addr0 for even). Unguarded and even-iface_num effects: IPV6_ADDR copies the address bytes into ipv6_addr1 or ipv6_addr0; IPV6_LINKLOCAL copies value[8..] into ipv6_if_id; IPV6_ROUTER copies into ipv6_dflt_rtr_addr; ADDR_AUTOCFG sets or clears the neighbor-discovery address-enable bit of ipv6_addtl_opts for ISCSI_IPV6_AUTOCFG_ND_ENABLE or ISCSI_IPV6_AUTOCFG_DISABLE and otherwise only logs an error; LINKLOCAL_AUTOCFG sets or clears the link-local autoconfig bit for its enable/disable values and otherwise logs an error; ROUTER_AUTOCFG zeroes ipv6_dflt_rtr_addr when value[0] is ISCSI_IPV6_ROUTER_AUTOCFG_ENABLE and does nothing otherwise; IFACE_ENABLE sets or clears the IPv6 protocol-enable bit of ipv6_opts and calls qla4xxx_create_ipv6_iface(ha) or qla4xxx_destroy_ipv6_iface(ha) respectively (ISCSI_IFACE_ENABLE selects create); VLAN_TAG stores the big-endian 16-bit value into ipv6_vlan_tag only when iface_param->len equals sizeof(ipv6_vlan_tag), else changes nothing; VLAN_ENABLED sets or clears the VLAN-tagging bit; MTU stores the little-endian 16-bit value into eth_mtu_size; PORT, FLOW_LABEL store 16-bit values (ipv6_port, ipv6_flow_lbl), TCP_WSF, IPV6_TRAFFIC_CLASS, IPV6_HOP_LIMIT and DUP_ADDR_DETECT_CNT store value[0], and ND_REACHABLE_TMO, ND_REXMIT_TIME, ND_STALE_TMO and RTR_ADV_LINK_MTU store a little-endian 32-bit value; DELAYED_ACK_EN, TCP_NAGLE_DISABLE and TCP_WSF_DISABLE set the corresponding disable bit of ipv6_tcp_opts when value[0] is ISCSI_NET_PARAM_DISABLE and clear it otherwise; TCP_TIMESTAMP_EN, GRAT_NEIGHBOR_ADV_EN, REDIRECT_EN and MLD_EN set their bit when value[0] is ISCSI_NET_PARAM_ENABLE and clear it otherwise; TCP_TIMER_SCALE clears the timer-scale field of ipv6_tcp_opts and ORs in (value[0] << 1) masked to the field. An unrecognised param only logs an error. The function reads 2-byte and 4-byte values through casts of iface_param->value, so value must be readable for that width. Apart from the create/destroy calls it takes no locks, takes no references and allocates or frees nothing.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: the PORT case has the odd iface_num guard at ql4_os.c:2139-2142 (the old prose already left PORT out of the unguarded list). Cases without the guard: IPV6_ADDR (2044), IFACE_ENABLE (2109), VLAN_TAG (2121), VLAN_ENABLED (2127), MTU (2135). Slice cut the head.

name: qla4xxx_set_ipv4
prose: Applies one iSCSI network parameter (iface_param->param, value, len, iface_num) to the IPv4 part of the address control block init_fw_cb; returns void (ql4_os.c:2284, slice cut the head). It is a switch with exactly one case taken. IPV4_ADDR, IPV4_SUBNET and IPV4_GW (memcpy into ipv4_addr, ipv4_subnet, ipv4_gw_addr), IPV4_BOOTPROTO, IFACE_ENABLE, VLAN_TAG, VLAN_ENABLED, MTU and PORT have no iface_num guard; every other recognised case does nothing when iface_param->iface_num is odd, including IPV4_DHCP_ALT_CLIENT_ID and IPV4_DHCP_VENDOR_ID. BOOTPROTO sets or clears the BOOTPROTO bit of ipv4_tcp_opts when value[0] is ISCSI_BOOTPROTO_DHCP or ISCSI_BOOTPROTO_STATIC and otherwise only logs an error, leaving the field unchanged. IFACE_ENABLE sets or clears the interface-enable bit of ipv4_ip_opts and calls qla4xxx_create_ipv4_iface(ha) (when value[0] is ISCSI_IFACE_ENABLE) or qla4xxx_destroy_ipv4_iface(ha). VLAN_TAG stores the big-endian 16-bit value into ipv4_vlan_tag only when iface_param->len equals sizeof(ipv4_vlan_tag). VLAN_ENABLED sets or clears the VLAN-tagging bit; MTU and PORT store little-endian 16-bit values into eth_mtu_size and ipv4_port. For the guarded cases: DELAYED_ACK_EN, TCP_NAGLE_DISABLE, TCP_WSF_DISABLE and FRAGMENT_DISABLE set their bit when value[0] is ISCSI_NET_PARAM_DISABLE and clear it otherwise; TCP_TIMESTAMP_EN, DHCP_DNS_ADDR_EN, DHCP_SLP_DA_EN, TOS_EN, GRAT_ARP_EN, DHCP_ALT_CLIENT_ID_EN, DHCP_REQ_VENDOR_ID_EN, DHCP_USE_VENDOR_ID_EN, DHCP_LEARN_IQN_EN, IN_FORWARD_EN and REDIRECT_EN set their bit when value[0] is ISCSI_NET_PARAM_ENABLE and clear it otherwise; TCP_WSF, TOS and TTL store value[0] into ipv4_tcp_wsf, ipv4_tos, ipv4_ttl; TCP_TIMER_SCALE clears the timer-scale field of ipv4_tcp_opts and ORs in (value[0] << 1) masked to the field. DHCP_ALT_CLIENT_ID and DHCP_VENDOR_ID copy sizeof(field) - 1 bytes into ipv4_dhcp_alt_cid or ipv4_dhcp_vid and set the matching length field to strlen of that field; the last byte of the field is not written by this function, so strlen relies on a NUL appearing in the copied bytes or already present in the last byte. An unrecognised param only logs an error. 2-byte values are read through a cast of iface_param->value. Apart from the create/destroy calls it takes no locks, takes no references and allocates or frees nothing.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: DHCP_ALT_CLIENT_ID and DHCP_VENDOR_ID do have the odd iface_num guard (ql4_os.c:2455-2456, 2483-2484). Round 2 right and already reflected: MTU (2337), PORT (2341), VLAN_ENABLED (2329), VLAN_TAG (2323) unguarded. Original claims (VLAN_TAG length mismatch 2324, bad BOOTPROTO 2301-2310 leave fields unchanged) right and stated. Corrected the old strlen precondition: the final byte of the field is not written (2457-2458, 2485-2486).

name: resp_mode_sense
prose: Builds the response to MODE SENSE(6) or MODE SENSE(10) for the scsi_debug device. Slice cut the head; real definition at scsi_debug.c:2955. It allocates a zeroed buffer of SDEBUG_MAX_MSENSE_SZ bytes on the heap with kzalloc(GFP_ATOMIC) held through a scope-based kfree, and returns -ENOMEM if that fails. It decodes DBD, page control (cmd[2] >> 6), page code, subpage code, LLBAA and the allocation length. A block descriptor of 8 bytes (16 with LLBAA on 10-byte commands) is requested only for disk, zoned or tape devices when DBD is clear. If page control is 3 (saved values) it sets illegal-request sense SAVING_PARAMS_UNSUP and returns check_condition_result. It then fills the mode parameter header (device-specific byte, with write-protect when sdebug_wp is set for disk/zoned devices), and for a nonzero block-descriptor length sets sdebug_capacity from get_sdebug_capacity() if it is zero and writes the block descriptor (a 16-byte descriptor on a tape device sets invalid-field-in-data sense and returns check_condition_result). If cmd[2] is 0 it skips the pages. Otherwise it switches on the page code to append pages (error recovery, disconnect-reconnect, format for disks only, caching for disk or zoned, control with subpages 0, 5 or 0xff, tape compression and partition pages for tape only, SAS pages with subpages, informational exceptions, or all pages for 0x3f); an unsupported subpage sets invalid-field-in-CDB sense for byte 3 and an unsupported or device-type-mismatched page code sets it for byte 2, in both cases returning check_condition_result. On success it writes the mode data length into the header (arr[0] for 6-byte, bytes 0-1 for 10-byte commands) and returns fill_from_dev_buffer(scp, arr, min(alloc_len, offset)), so the result can be shorter than the full response. The buffer is freed automatically on every return that follows the allocation.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: the buffer is heap-allocated with kzalloc(GFP_ATOMIC) and returns -ENOMEM on failure (scsi_debug.c:2964-2970), freed by the __free(kfree) annotation at scope exit. Slice cut the head.

name: resp_read_tape
prose: Simulated tape READ(6). Slice cut the head; real definition at scsi_debug.c:4463. Starting position pos is devip->tape_location[tape_partition]. (1) If cmd[0] is not READ_6 it builds invalid-opcode sense and returns illegal_condition_result. (2) FIXED is cmd[1] bit 0 and SILI is bit 1; if both are set it builds invalid-field-in-CDB sense (byte 1) and returns check_condition_result. (3) transfer is the 24-bit value in cmd[2..4]; if FIXED, num = transfer blocks of size devip->tape_blksize; otherwise num is 1 and size = transfer, and a transfer outside TAPE_MIN_BLKSIZE..TAPE_MAX_BLKSIZE builds invalid-field-in-CDB sense (byte 2) and returns check_condition_result. (4) The loop runs while i < num and pos < tape_eop[partition]. Each iteration first sets tape_location[partition] to pos + 1, then examines the block: a filemark block builds NO_SENSE filemark-detected sense (information fixed ? num - i : size, flag FILEMARK), sets residue (num - i) * size and returns check_condition_result with tape_location left at pos + 1; an end-of-data block builds BLANK_CHECK EOD-detected sense (same information rule), sets tape_location back to pos, sets residue (num - i) * size and returns check_condition_result. Only if the block is neither filemark nor EOD does it zero size bytes of the data buffer at offset i * size and copy the block's 4 data bytes there. Then, if FIXED and the block's fl_size differs from tape_blksize, it sets residue (num - i) * size, builds an ILI sense with information num - i and returns check_condition_result; if not FIXED and fl_size differs from size, it sets residue size - fl_size when fl_size < size, and if SILI is clear builds ILI sense with information size - fl_size and returns check_condition_result (a longer block gets this too), while with SILI set the loop carries on. (5) After the loop, if pos >= tape_eop[partition] (which is also true when the loop consumed exactly the last block, not only when it stopped early) it builds NO_SENSE EOP/EOM sense (information fixed ? num - i : size, flag EOM), sets tape_location[partition] to pos - 1 and returns check_condition_result. (6) Otherwise it sets tape_location[partition] to pos and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the zero-fill/copy (scsi_debug.c:4518-4521) comes after the filemark (4502-4508) and EOD (4510-4517) checks; old prose said before any check. Round 2 right (longer block with SILI clear gives ILI, 4531-4539, now stated). Original right (illegal_condition_result at 4475, location updates at 4501/4514/4547). Also noted: the EOP check at 4543 uses pos >= eop even after a full read.

name: scsi_result_to_blk_status
prose: Maps a SCSI result word to a blk_status_t; the slice cut the head, the function is static blk_status_t scsi_result_to_blk_status(int result) at scsi_lib.c:715. It first switches on the mid-layer status byte, which is bits 8 to 15 of result (scsi_ml_byte, (result >> 8) & 0xff): value SCSIML_STAT_RESV_CONFLICT (1) returns BLK_STS_RESV_CONFLICT, SCSIML_STAT_NOSPC (2) returns BLK_STS_NOSPC, SCSIML_STAT_MED_ERROR (3) returns BLK_STS_MEDIUM, SCSIML_STAT_TGT_FAILURE (4) returns BLK_STS_TARGET, SCSIML_STAT_DL_TIMEOUT (5) returns BLK_STS_DURATION_LIMIT; value 0 (SCSIML_STAT_OK) and any other value fall through to the next step. It then switches on the host byte, bits 16 to 23 of result: DID_OK (0x00) returns BLK_STS_OK if scsi_status_is_good(result) is true and BLK_STS_IOERR otherwise; DID_TRANSPORT_FAILFAST (0x0f) and DID_TRANSPORT_MARGINAL (0x14) return BLK_STS_TRANSPORT; every other host byte returns BLK_STS_IOERR. scsi_status_is_good(result) is false for a negative result and for host byte DID_NO_CONNECT; otherwise it masks the low status byte with 0xfe and is true for SAM_STAT_GOOD (0x00), CONDITION_MET (0x04), INTERMEDIATE (0x10), INTERMEDIATE_CONDITION_MET (0x14) and COMMAND_TERMINATED (0x22), and false for all other values including CHECK_CONDITION (0x02). The function only reads its argument and takes no locks or references.
note: Old prose wrong on two counts: the mid-layer byte is bits 8-15 not 24-31 (scsi_priv.h:33-36), and the 'good' status set is 0x00/0x04/0x10/0x14/0x22 (scsi.h:202-223 with scsi_proto.h:201-212), not including CHECK_CONDITION 0x02. Round 2: right that 16-23 is the host byte and CHECK_CONDITION is not good, but its 24-31 claim for the mid-layer byte is also wrong. Round 15: right (0x02 listed wrongly, 0x22 missing). Round 1 (contract constrains input) moot: contract field empty.

name: blk_rq_err_bytes
note: No function named blk_rq_err_bytes exists in this tree (no match under block/, include/, drivers/scsi/, drivers/block/) and the slice scsi_lib.c:768-1064 contains scsi_cmd_runtime_exceeced (789), scsi_io_completion_action (815) and scsi_io_completion_nz_result (998), not this one; the listed item is not a function defined in the code.

name: spi_print_msg
prose: Prints a SCSI parallel-interface message at msg to the kernel log with printk and returns its length in bytes; it does not write to msg and takes no locks. There are two definitions selected by CONFIG_SCSI_CONSTANTS (scsi_transport_spi.c:1287 with constants, 1351 without); both compute the same return value len, starting from 1. If msg[0] is EXTENDED_MESSAGE, len = 2 + msg[1], and 258 when msg[1] is 0 (len == 2 gets 256 added). If msg[0] is not extended: values with bit 0x80 set (identify), values below 0x1f, and 0x55 give len 1; values from 0x1f up to 0x2f give len 2 and read msg[1] (so 0x1f is treated as a two-byte message); other values give len 1. Readability needed: at least 1 byte; msg[1] for 0x1f..0x2f; for an extended message msg[1] and, in the CONFIG_SCSI_CONSTANTS variant, msg[2] and then at least len bytes (258 when msg[1] is 0) without the constants variant (which prints msg[0..len-1] as hex), and with the constants variant the decoders read: 7 bytes for EXTENDED_MODIFY_DATA_POINTER (msg[3..6]), 5 for EXTENDED_SDTR (msg[3], msg[4]), 4 for EXTENDED_WDTR (msg[3]), 7 for EXTENDED_PPR (msg[3], msg[5], msg[6]), 11 for EXTENDED_MODIFY_BIDI_DATA_PTR (msg[3..10]), and for any other extended code the bytes msg[2..len-1] printed in hex. Output: with CONFIG_SCSI_CONSTANTS the message is decoded into names (one-byte, two-byte and extended message names, identify fields, "QAS Request" for 0x55, reserved forms otherwise, with decoded period, offset, width or pointers for extended messages); without it the raw bytes are printed in hex.
note: Round 15 right: EXTENDED_PPR calls print_nego(msg, 3, 5, 6) (scsi_transport_spi.c:1310) which reads msg[6], so 7 bytes are needed, not 6. Round 2 right: 0x1f falls in the two-byte branch (1335, 1368) and returns 2. Round 1 right: the non-CONSTANTS variant prints hex only (1351-1374); prose now distinguishes both variants. Old precondition also omitted that msg[2] is read for any extended message in the constants variant (1294).

name: sr_cd_check
prose: Probes a CD-ROM drive for multisession information; the packet name sr_get_last_session does not exist, the function is int sr_cd_check(struct cdrom_device_info *cdi) at sr_vendor.c:171 and the slice shows only its WRITER case and tail. Returns 0 immediately, with no allocation, if CDC_MULTI_SESSION is already set in cd->cdi.mask. Otherwise it kmallocs a 512-byte buffer (-ENOMEM on failure), and switches on cd->vendor to issue a vendor-specific read of the last session start with sr_do_ioctl: VENDOR_SCSI3 (READ_TOC, 12 bytes), VENDOR_NEC (0xde command), VENDOR_TOSHIBA (0xc7 command, which also calls sr_set_blocklength(cd, 2048)), VENDOR_WRITER (READ_TOC first for 4 bytes; if buffer[2] is 0 it logs 'No finished session' and leaves rc at 0; otherwise a second READ_TOC for the last session number buffer[2] & 0x7f, 12 bytes), and any other vendor logs an unknown-vendor warning, sets sector 0 and no_multi. A failing sr_do_ioctl stops that case with sector still 0 and rc holding its nonzero result (for TOSHIBA, -EINVAL also sets no_multi); a response judged to mean the drive lacks multisession support (short SCSI3 TOC, NEC buffer[14] other than 0 or 0xb0) sets no_multi; the SCSI3 case also sets sector 0 when buffer[6] is 1 or less. After the switch it sets cd->ms_offset to sector, sets cd->xa_flag to 1 only if sr_disk_status(cdi) is not CDS_AUDIO and sr_is_xa(cd) returns 1 (else 0), calls sr_set_blocklength(cd, 2048) (result ignored) if cd->device->sector_size is not 2048, sets CDC_MULTI_SESSION in cdi->mask when no_multi is set, frees the buffer and returns rc. rc is 0 on success and for the default-vendor and 'no finished session' cases, and the nonzero result of the failing sr_do_ioctl otherwise; it is never the value of buffer[2] at return (in the WRITER case rc = buffer[2] is overwritten by the second ioctl's result when buffer[2] is nonzero). The ms_offset, xa_flag and block-length steps run on every path that reaches the end of the switch, including after ioctl failures.
note: Name was wrong: real function sr_cd_check (sr_vendor.c:171-340). Old prose wrongly said it returns the positive buffer[2] for 'no finished session': at sr_vendor.c:291-295 rc = buffer[2] == 0 there, and a nonzero buffer[2] is overwritten by the second sr_do_ioctl at 305. Also the early return at 179-180 (CDC_MULTI_SESSION already set) was missing. Rejection reasons were mechanical only.

name: st_set_options
prose: Applies an MTSETDRVBUFFER-style option word to a tape device; slice cut the head, real definition at st.c:2301. STm is STp->modes[STp->current_mode]. If that mode is not yet defined it copies mode 0 into it (keeping STm's own cdevs[] and devs[] pointers) and sets the global modes_defined to 1. It then dispatches on code = options & MT_ST_OPTIONS: MT_ST_BOOLEANS assigns each flag (buffer writes, async writes, default writes, read ahead, two filemarks, fast MTEOM, auto lock, can_bsr, omit block limits, can_partitions only if the device scsi_level is at least SCSI_2, SCSI-2 logical, immediate, immediate filemark, sysv, sili) from the corresponding bit; MT_ST_SETBOOLEANS or MT_ST_CLEARBOOLEANS sets or clears only the flags whose bits are present in options; MT_ST_WRITE_THRESHOLD does nothing; MT_ST_DEF_BLKSIZE sets STm->default_blksize to the low bits (-1 when they are all ones) and, for a value other than that, when STp->ready is ST_READY also clears blksize_changed and calls set_mode_densblk; MT_ST_TIMEOUTS sets STp->long_timeout (value without MT_ST_SET_LONG_TIMEOUT, times HZ) when that flag is present, otherwise sets the request queue timeout with blk_queue_rq_timeout to value * HZ; MT_ST_SET_CLN takes value = low byte of the argument, returns -EINVAL if value is nonzero and below EXTENDED_SENSE_START or at or above SCSI_SENSE_BUFFERSIZE, otherwise stores cln_mode, cln_sense_mask (bits 8-15) and cln_sense_value (bits 16-23); MT_ST_DEF_OPTIONS handles the sub-codes MT_ST_DEF_DENSITY, MT_ST_DEF_DRVBUFFER and MT_ST_DEF_COMPRESSION (setting or, with MT_ST_CLEAR_DEFAULT, clearing the defaults, with side calls to set_mode_densblk, st_int_ioctl(MTSETDRVBUFFER) and st_compression when STp->ready is ST_READY) and an unrecognised sub-code does nothing and still returns 0. Any other code returns -EIO. The returns are therefore 0, -EINVAL (only from MT_ST_SET_CLN) and -EIO (unrecognised code); no other path returns -EINVAL, and the results of set_mode_densblk, st_int_ioctl and st_compression are not checked. No locks are taken here.
note: Rounds 2 and 15 wrong: there is no -EINVAL for an invalid default block size, drive-buffer or compression subcode; the only -EINVAL is in MT_ST_SET_CLN (st.c:2412-2415), the DEF_BLKSIZE/DEF_OPTIONS branches (2384-2475) have no error return, and unknown DEF_OPTIONS subcodes fall through to return 0 (2479). Original claim (non-boolean options handled) right and already covered. Slice cut the head.

name: st_int_ioctl
prose: Issues one internal tape ioctl command cmd_in with argument arg to the drive and updates the cached position; slice cut the head, real definition at st.c:2724 (full function read). Requires STp->buffer->do_dio == 0 (WARN_ON otherwise). If STp->ready is ST_NO_TAPE it returns -ENOMEDIUM and if it is any other value except ST_READY it returns -EIO. It copies the current partition's drv_file, drv_block and at_sm into local fileno, blkno and at_sm and builds a CDB by a switch on cmd_in. Early returns from the switch: -EACCES for MTWEOF, MTWEOFI, MTWSM and MTERASE when STp->write_prot is set; 0 for MTNOP (no command); for MTSETBLK, MTSETDENSITY, MTSETDRVBUFFER and SET_DENS_AND_BLK, -EIO if STp->dirty is set or the buffer holds data, and -EINVAL (MTSETBLK and SET_DENS_AND_BLK only) when a nonzero block size in arg is outside STp->min_block..STp->max_block while STp->max_block > 0; -ENOSYS for any other cmd_in; and for MTEOM with !STp->fast_mteom, after a recursive st_int_ioctl(MTFSF, 0x7fffff), it sets fileno from STps->drv_file and returns 0 immediately if STps->eof >= ST_EOD_1, so the MTEOM position write-back below is skipped on that path (the recursive call's own write-back has already run). For the other commands the local position is updated in advance: MTFSF/MTFSFM add arg to fileno only if fileno >= 0 and set blkno to 0; MTBSF/MTBSFM subtract arg from fileno only if fileno >= 0 and set blkno to -1; MTFSR adds arg to blkno only if blkno >= 0; MTBSR subtracts arg only if blkno >= 0; MTFSS/MTBSS set fileno and blkno to -1 and at_sm to 1 when arg is nonzero; MTWEOF/MTWEOFI/MTWSM add arg to fileno only if fileno >= 0, set blkno to 0 and at_sm to 1 only for MTWSM; MTREW and MTRETEN set all three to 0; MTEOM sets blkno to -1, at_sm to 0 and fileno to -1 when fast_mteom is set. It then runs the CDB with st_do_scsi; if that returns NULL it returns STp->buffer->syscall_result without writing back position. If the result is 0 it releases the request, stores blkno, fileno and at_sm into the partition, and for MTBSFM and MTFSFM then runs a recursive MTFSF or MTBSF with arg 1 and uses its result as the return value (MTFSFM and MTBSFM are first executed directly as the same SPACE command as MTFSF and MTBSF, not replaced by the recursive call); for the mode-select commands it updates block_size (and buffer_blocks, buffer_bytes, read_pointer), density or drv_buffer; it sets STps->eof to ST_EOD for MTEOM, ST_FM for MTFSF, or ST_NOEOF when chg_eof is set (chg_eof is cleared for MTFSFM, MTBSFM and the mode-select commands), and STps->rw to ST_IDLE for MTWEOF and MTWEOFI. If the result is nonzero it uses the sense data: SENSE_EOM sets eof to ST_EOM_OK (except for MTBSF, MTBSFM, MTBSR, MTBSS) and drv_block to 0; MTWEOF/MTWEOFI with sense and SENSE_EOM return 0 with eof ST_NOEOF when the sense key is NO_SENSE or RECOVERED_ERROR, else adjust fileno by the undone count; MTFSF/MTFSFM, MTBSF/MTBSFM, MTFSR, MTBSR and MTEOM each adjust drv_file, drv_block and eof as in lines 3060-3101 (MTEOM sets both to -1 and eof to ST_EOD); for a mode-select command with ILLEGAL_REQUEST, ASC 0x24, scsi_level <= SCSI_2 and PF not yet tested it toggles use_pf, releases the request and returns the result of a recursive st_int_ioctl retry; any BLANK_CHECK sense sets eof to ST_EOD. The request is released in every nonzero-result path except the recursive-retry path, which releases it first, and the function returns ioctl_result (the nonzero SCSI result unless changed to 0 by the MTWEOF/MTWEOFI EOM case).
